operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Section 1. There is established the Hopi-Navajo Land Settlement 
Interagency Committee (hereinafter referred to as the Committee). The 
membership of the Committee shall consist of the Secretary of the Interior, 
who shall be its Chairman, the Attorney General, the Secretary of Agri­
culture, the Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of Labor, the Secre­
tary of Health, Education, and Welfare, and the Secretary of Housing 
and Urban Development.

source.quoted_text:
By virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 1(c)(2)  of the 
Act to provide for final settlement of the conflicting rights and interests 
of the Hopi and Navajo Tribes concerning lands within the reservation 
established by the Executive order of December 16, 1882, and lands 
within the reservation created by the Act of June 14, 1934, and for 
other purposes (Public Law 93— 531, approved December 22, 1974, 
hereinafter referred to as the A ct), and as President of the United States 
of America, Section 2(a)  of Executive Order No. 11829 of January 6, 
1975, is hereby amended to read as follows:
“ Sec. 2. Functions of the Committee, (a.)  The Committee shall, to 
the extent permitted by law, and as provided by Section 1(c)(2)  of the 
Act, develop relevant information for and respond to the requests of the 
Mediator who shall be appointed by the Director of the Federal Media­
tion and Conciliation Service pursuant to Section 1(a)  of the Act, in 
order to facilitate the expeditious and orderly compilation and develop­
ment of factual information relevant to the negotiation process estab­
lished by the Act.”

research_rationale: This is a partial source-read candidate preserving provisional NO. The full held official-source extracts of EO 11829 (40 FR 1497), EO 11853 (40 FR 17537), and EO 12379 (47 FR 36099-36100) were read; the recorded PDF hashes have matching GPO fixity rows. Seven exact original spans separately preserve sections 2(a), 2(b), the committee termination condition, the Mediator notice, and the records transfer. EO 11853 immediately rewrites section 2(a), clarifying the information-development role in the negotiation process. EO 12379 section 11 immediately revokes EO 11829 as amended, without a deferred effective date elsewhere in the actor; August 17, 1982 is a formal later revocation event, not the proven first end. EO 11829 section 4 expressly selects completion of statutory Mediator duties as its earlier termination trigger. The unavailable statute/occurrence evidence and unclosed notice/record-transfer commands prevent a complete lifecycle or blanket no-residual finding. No deadline, machine chain date, or editorial disposition is substituted for the missing event.
unresolved_material_gaps: Actual original, amending and revoking PDF page images were not present at the cited cache locations and were not inspected. GPO fixity rows match the recorded PDF hashes; exact held OCR is not an authenticated page transcription.

EO 11829 section 4 ties termination to completion of the Mediator duties as determined under Public Law 93-531 section 1(a). The controlling statute and evidence of actual completion are not held in the inspected packet/search results. No original clause first-end or whole_order_end date is asserted.

EO 11853 replaced section 2(a) on April 17, 1975 using immediate amendment wording. Earlier cessation under section 4 and the statute has not been ruled out; the amendment is a later event only, with the complete replacement text retained in its source.

Section 4 separately requires the Mediator to advise the Chairman when duties cease and directs transfer of Committee records to the Secretary of the Interior. Actual notice, transfer, and any independent continuing records obligations have not been established; these commands cannot be dismissed with committee termination.

The held machine searches do not determine the historical triggering occurrence or records transfer. U.S. Code coverage stops at 2026-10-09, leaving cutoff coverage through 2026-10-14 unclosed. later_source_search remains empty.

The claim-kit chain misattributes EO 12379 language to ten other orders and their dates. These associations are rejected from the full actor text; target EDGES rows identify only EO 11853 and EO 12379. No exhaustive negative earlier-history finding is made.
